study.question: Does allowing each feedback task to choose its own action-aware history relevance improve the equal-weight four-task validation AUC, relative to one shared summary, without changing the supplied information or training recipe?
study.hypothesis: Source inspection of baseline-din shows one item-only local-activation score per historical exposure, shared by all tasks; historical action is only a pooled value. This imposes identical relative history weights before the separate towers. A shared nonlinear scorer with task-specific output rows and historical-action input may preserve common target/item structure while learning different evidence selection for the four tasks. This is a representational bottleneck hypothesis, not an observed negative-transfer result: baseline-din macro AUC=0.8099233880793816, with click/cart/fav/buy AUC=0.6555440824200336/0.8490697019534956/0.8648974928883688/0.8701822750556283. Empty-history macro=0.7268428930232654 (6444 samples) versus >64-history macro=0.8273443710421104 (1401885 samples) motivates history diagnostics but is confounded by population and prevalence. No gradient conflict or feedback-composition diagnostic has been measured.

nearest_work.difference: Archived primary text arXiv:1706.06978v4 lines250-277 describes target-conditioned unnormalized weighted history aggregation. Retain that mechanism, field adaptation and Dice, but let historical actions enter the scoring trunk and let task-indexed score rows determine separate summaries. This is an adaptation study, not a DIN invention or exact paper reproduction.

Pinned benchmark source lines123-169 initializes task-specific sequence hubs with action masks and updates categorical/sequence/task representations through aggregation and broadcasts (lines204-219). The proposed one-stage scorer keeps all valid feedback available to every task, shares the relevance trunk, and isolates task routing from action input in a 2x2 design. No hub initialization, layered broadcast, or imported result. Original paper:infnet resolves to link-only metadata; its detailed text is unavailable and no stronger novelty comparison is claimed.

Pinned benchmark forward lines107-142 evolves nonsequential queries and then averages tokens to give each task a shared bottom representation. Our study instead isolates task participation at history aggregation while keeping the existing field/tower pipeline. It does not implement query mixing or repeated retrieval, and does not claim improvement over MixFormer.

Authorized section2.3 describes task/hub and joint-query families; it is a nearest-work map, not evidence of local effectiveness or complete original-method audit. No general priority or novelty claim is made.

study.proposed_difference: Allocate a shared local-activation trunk with input [target,history,target-history,target*history,historical_action] and four score rows indexed by feature_map.labels. Route score t to tower t (T1) or average the four scores and broadcast the same score to all towers (T0). Supply action embeddings to the scorer (A1) or zero only those input columns (A0). Values include item and action embeddings in all cells, so A0 still observes feedback through values. All cells construct identical tensors/modules and copy the first initialized output row to all four rows, removing initial shared-vs-task score-scale differences. Explicitly zero masked keys/actions before Dice and mask scores after scoring in every cell. No task-history hard filtering, label-derived input, additional data, training-loss modification, softmax, new optimizer or extra passes. Nominal dense count is baseline266213+16*64+3*(32+1)=267336, total32060552 with inherited embedding count31793216; analytical, host verification pending. T0 has redundant output rows; A0 has inactive action columns, so nominal matching is not effective-capacity matching.
predictions: Primary prospective prediction: validation macro_auc(task_action_relevance) > macro_auc(shared_action_relevance), with every task AUC/Logloss delta reported against both that control and baseline-din. Select the incumbent across baseline-din and all four new variants using the frozen macro-AUC rule, then macro Logloss, parameters and trial ID. No per-task veto or post-hoc score weights.

Action contribution prediction: macro_auc(task_action_relevance) > macro_auc(task_item_relevance). Evaluate the task contrast also at A0 and action contrast also at T0. Report the interaction [AUC(T1,A1)-AUC(T0,A1)]-[AUC(T1,A0)-AUC(T0,A0)]; positive interaction is predicted but not required for a main task-routing effect.

If benefits involve differentiated evidence selection, learned task score patterns may differ and gains may occur on nonempty histories. Host slice AUC alone cannot establish attention specialization, causal sharing, gradient-conflict reduction or negative-transfer mitigation; those need authorized follow-up diagnostics. No unavailable diagnostics are assumed.

Reuse predeclared history bins empty/1-16/17-64/>64. Report samples, positives, negatives, per-task AUC/Logloss and full-data deltas; mark slices with <100 positives or <100 negatives as insufficient for confirmatory interpretation. Empty-history positives45/28/13 for the auxiliary tasks already imply insufficiency. Length bins are diagnostic, not separate selection criteria.

Only validation is authorized. Where host capabilities permit, later repetitions use three paired seeds with frozen variants and paired user-cluster bootstrap; current one-seed factorial outcomes remain preliminary. Do not independently bootstrap impressions or request held-out outputs.
falsifiers: Task-routing contrast is nonpositive at A1 and A0, or any apparent gain fails paired-seed follow-up: no support for useful task-specific aggregation in this implementation. Do not call this a universal refutation of task conditioning.
T1/A1 fails to exceed T1/A0 and the action contrasts/interaction are nonpositive: historical action at scoring time is unsupported, even if task-specific item scoring succeeds.
Only shared controls improve over baseline-din, while T1 does not beat matched T0: attribute the family gain to the shared scorer/parameterization or common masking changes, not task participation.

Required host checks fail for finite outputs/backward, mask perturbation invariance, all-empty histories or all-four-output identity/shapes, or a trial exceeds1208.5413760878146s: retain the failure and cost, repair only within the same frozen protocol before interpretation.
A single-seed gain or different learned attention scores without controlled repeated predictive gains is insufficient evidence for reduced negative transfer, a causal mechanism or broad originality.
alternative_explanations: Task-specific routing changes effective expressivity and gradient coupling despite identical nominal parameter counts; shared averaging is algebraically a single-output scorer with redundant parameters. No exact capacity isolation or pure negative-transfer claim.

A0 zero action columns have no predictive training gradients, while A1 columns are active. The factorial isolates action access, not active capacity. Action may function mainly as a behavior-frequency proxy under the released offline feedback policy.

Dice uses batch statistics over the fixed100 positions; explicit zeroing blocks masked-ID dependence but padding counts and repeated target values still influence those statistics. This is shared by the four variants and differs in masking implementation from baseline-din.

Although all cells start from identical channel functions and matched module shapes, averaging changes scorer gradient magnitudes and optimizer trajectories. Baseline also has a different scorer initialization shape. No warm starts or learning-rate tuning to hide these differences.

Observed slice differences can reflect user mix, label prevalence, training frequency and history length rather than a history mechanism. No feedback-composition, frequency, hour or missing-field slices are available in the current receipt; do not fabricate them.

Rare auxiliary labels, one data pass and one initial seed can cause estimation noise or optimization failure. Auxiliary labels are category/brand matches within24h, not advertisement-specific conversion; official_offline history maturity and whole-window vocabulary limitations remain.

variants.name: task_action_relevance
variants.note: Factorial T1/A1. Each prediction task receives its own target/action-conditioned weighted history. Shared embeddings, scorer trunk and sum-four-BCE training remain. No efficacy or originality claim before host execution.

variants.name: shared_action_relevance
variants.note: Factorial T0/A1. Average all four scorer channels and route that same history summary to every tower; isolates task-specific routing with action-aware scoring. Same initial channel functions and nominal parameter count; reduced effective capacity is an explicit confound.

variants.name: task_item_relevance
variants.note: Factorial T1/A0. Replace scorer action embeddings by zero; historical actions remain in pooled values. Isolates scorer access to feedback while retaining task routing, parameter count and dense layer shapes.

variants.name: shared_item_relevance
variants.note: Factorial T0/A0. Both interventions off. Closest matched family control; compare with baseline-din to reveal effects of changed initialization, output parameterization and explicit masking. Does not constitute an exact baseline rerun.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Used its inspected task-aware aggregation idea as nearest-work motivation for an early task-specific history readout, rather than copying a full architecture or accepting external effectiveness. Baseline source is the empirical reason for testing that location.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: One shared DIN relevance trunk with task-indexed score rows and action-aware input; keep every valid feedback accessible to each task. This deliberately omits task-mask hub pooling, iterative hub exchange and gated broadcasts.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: Relative to pinned INFNet implementation, a one-stage controlled task/action relevance factorization without hub tokens or layered field/sequence/task broadcasting. Original method full-paper details unresolved; no novelty claim.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: No positive task-routing contrast after matched action controls and paired repetitions, or gains confined to shared controls.

knowledge_assessments.rationale: Inspected evolving-query and shared-bottom forward path. Repeated sequence/field refinement is not identified by the present baseline diagnostics and would add interacting changes before task participation is tested.
knowledge_assessments.transformed_mechanism: None adopted; retain as a possible future whole-model alternative after task-readout evidence.
knowledge_assessments.nearest_work_difference: Current candidate keeps a single target-conditioned retrieval stage and task-specific summaries, not iterative query mixing/cross-attention with a shared averaged bottom.
knowledge_assessments.falsifier: A later budget-matched repeated-query control could show that evolving field queries, rather than task-specific history weights, explain the useful signal.
